meal.title: Create an object from a class (instantiate)
meal.objective: Instantiate an object using the class name and store it in a variable

voice.script: What if you could turn a blueprint into a real car in seconds? Imagine a car company’s factory line: the blueprint defines the car, the car itself is the object. How do you create a usable car from the blueprint? First, Python lets you turn a class into an actual object called an instance. An instance is the actual car built from the class blueprint. To do that, you write the class name followed by parentheses and assign it to a variable. Now we write the code to create an instance. For example, we define a Student class with a name attribute, then create a student object by calling Student with a name and storing it in a variable called alice. Running the program prints the student’s name. Creating an instance brings a class to life. Try making another Student object with a different name.
